text: It’s always nice to come back to BCU whenever there’s an opportunity and yesterday I had the chance to be one of the industry panellists at an event organised by the BCU Women In STEM Society We covered a lot during the panel, from degree vs experience and whether AI is a threat or an opportunity, to the power of networking and the challenges and mistakes we’ve faced so far. My biggest takeaway was the importance of networking. The connections you make can lead to opportunities and advice you simply wouldn't be able to find online. It was great to meet the students who came along. I also found myself really invested in the other panellists’ comments and points of view (Sania Akthar, Tyrese Edwards, Dawar P, Gibril Khalil, Yi wang) and took away plenty of useful tips and insights myself.

Last week I attended the Engineering & Developer Conference at Birmingham Tech Week 2026 with fellow BCU KTP Associates Nissy Joseph and Anish Ravikiran What I took away most was the chance to connect with people across the industry and hear from CEOs, heads of engineering and professionals with years of experience. A big theme throughout the day was how AI is changing the way we work. Speakers talked about the processes it’s speeding up, the risks that come with it and how it’s already reshaping what companies look for when hiring. Another topic that stood out was AI agents, from making APIs ready for them to embedding them safely within an organisation by controlling what they can do, not just what they’re told. As someone working on digital transformation in manufacturing, that’s definitely something worth digging into further.

Back in February I shared that I was one of three winners of the Cal Henderson Innovation Seed Fund. That funding let me take CombiLive back home to Lima and test it on the streets with a real combi driver and this video shows how it went 😆 For anyone who hasn’t seen my previous posts, CombiLive is a real-time tracking app for Lima’s combis, the privately run buses most of the city relies on for transportation every day. Drivers share their live location from their own phones, no extra hardware needed. Passengers can see where their bus is and get an ETA. If something goes wrong, the driver can press an emergency button that sends their exact location to an admin dashboard. Once fully deployed, the idea is for those alerts to go straight to the nearest police or emergency services. In the video I spent the day with José, who has worked the La Colonial route between Lima and La Punta for 35 years. He talked me through what the job is really like, from safety on board to passengers not knowing which combi to take. Then we put CombiLive to work in his combi while I followed behind, confirming the accurate live tracking and later waited at a stop, watching it come towards me in real time from the mobile app. Seeing it run on a real route with a real driver was the best way to close this chapter of the project. Thanks to José for sharing his experience and taking part in the video. Thanks also to Sara Hassan and Rehan Bhana at Birmingham City University for all the support behind the scenes and to my supervisor Waldo C. for his guidance. 🙌🙌

Last week I spent four days at Ashorne Hill - The home of Ashorne Advantage for the Project Management and Leadership module, part of the KTP Associate Training As KTP Associates we get the opportunity to attend two in-person training modules alongside other associates from all over the UK and this one was genuinely valuable and enjoyable. Our facilitator Rich Tricker played a huge part in that, making every session smooth, engaging and full of learning. 23 of us turned up not knowing each other, all from different backgrounds and working on different projects. By the end of the week we’d shared plenty of meals, swapped contacts, had a lot of laughs and worked through group activities that each had a takeaway we could apply back in our own roles. One topic that really stuck with me was influencing styles. As it was being explained, so much of it made sense based on situations I’ve already come across. Assertiveness is usually the go-to, but depending on the context you might reason with facts and numbers, bargain, share a vision or persuade, with leverage usually kept as a last resort when nothing else works. It’s definitely something I’ll be more conscious of in my day to day at ECAM. Already looking forward to the next module in January!!!!!

Officially two months in as Digital Transformation and AI Integration Engineer | KTP Associate at ECAM Engineering Limited & Birmingham City University 🫡 It’s taken me a little while to post this update. The first few weeks came with plenty of challenges outside of work. I moved to a new city on my own, commuting from Birmingham while I waited for my room, sorting out car paperwork (plus a flat tyre on moving day) and getting my Global Talent Visa application accepted. All sorted now and I’m properly settled in Stoke-on-Trent. Last Friday was my first Local Management Committee (LMC) meeting, where ECAM, BCU and Innovate UK come together to review the progress of the KTP. The feedback on what’s been delivered so far was really positive. I have to thank my BCU academics Dalia El-Banna and Waldo C. for their guidance. I’m also really grateful to philip arme, Tom Arme, Elliot Arme and Joshua Green for welcoming me into the ECAM family and to the operators on the shop floor for being so collaborative. Some highlights from the first two months - Gained hands-on experience with FANUC FOCAS programming to pull real-time data from a CNC machine - Built a first prototype of a CNC downtime monitoring dashboard that combines live machine data with operator input to give the full picture - Delivered a sustainability talk at BCU for a new foundation engineering course, showing how ECAM’s sustainable practices benefit both the environment and the business financially. Thanks to Jean-Baptiste R. G. Souppez for the opportunity Looking forward to sharing more updates during this new journey 😁😁

I graduated last week and I'm still reliving the day It was great to graduate alongside my friends and to hear that so many of them have got exciting plans ahead. I didn't really feel nervous until I was on stage, but seeing familiar faces in the audience, the academics sitting in the middle clapping and friends cheering even though my family weren't able to come and me thinking that I was "alone" when I really wasn't. Straight after I crossed the stage I checked my messages from my family who were watching the livestream and were living it as if they were there with me, which was very comforting. I wish all the best to my classmates now graduates that I met along the way and I'm sure they'll succeed in whatever they set their mind on. Hopefully we can stay in touch. As a side note, I'd like to share that I've secured a role as a KTP Associate in Digital Transformation and AI Integration at ECAM Engineering, in partnership with BCU and supported by Innovate UK. I'm excited and can't wait to start this role next week. I'll do a proper post once I'm settled and keep you posted on this KTP journey 🫡

Officially a Computer Science graduate now. First Class Honours, 78.48% 4 years at Birmingham City University, mostly spent trying to juggle job and uni. Went from endless shifts as a kitchen porter, to helping my sister open her own coffee shop, doing food events and travelling to new countries, to eventually working as a software developer during my placement year and as a teaching assistant. I was also lucky that every year turned out memorable: First year: best entrepreneurial project as a team Second year: Santander pitch award, 4th place overall and got to go to China as a BCU Ambassador Placement year: presented my placement experience through a poster and judged first year projects Final year: 1st place for Computing Final Year Project poster, judged first year projects again and got the Cal Henderson seed fund Thanks to everyone I met along the way who kept me motivated, the quality time and ultimately made the whole process fun. 🫡

Just like that, my last week and my last Innovation Festival at BCU as a Computer Science student I got to go on stage and receive the Computing Final Year Project Poster First Place award and honestly I was not expecting it at all. Everything felt surreal. Then I got called up a second time as one of the Cal Henderson Seed Fund winners, which was the cherry on top. But what really made my night was sharing it with all my friends and the academic staff who have been with me since first year. I came to the UK and started at BCU when I was 17. Excited to share this video the BCU marketing team put together featuring my Final Year Project at Innovation Festival 2026 CombiLive is a real-time bus tracking app I built for Lima, Peru, where most buses have no tracking, no journey planning and limited safety mechanisms once on the bus. The app lets drivers broadcast their live location, passengers plan journeys with traffic-aware ETAs, and administrators monitor their fleet and emergency alerts in real time, a low-cost solution with no dedicated hardware required. The Cal Henderson Seed Fund made it possible to take CombiLive to the next level, from a university project to a system actually tested on the streets of Lima. Really grateful to Armeen Mashini and Mia Osborne for reaching out and giving me this opportunity. The video came out amazing!!! The video is attached to this post and also available on Birmingham City University's YouTube channel: https://lnkd.in/eHAN6SdS Also I wanted to add that this is my final week at BCU and I am now actively looking for graduate opportunities in computing. I am open to roles across software development, mobile development and systems engineering, anywhere I can get hands-on and keep building things. If you know about any of those opportunities, please do let me know. 🫡

On Monday, I had the opportunity to present my final year project poster as an Innovation Seed Fund winner during a special visit from Cal Henderson to Birmingham City University. It was great to hear Cal speak and see how approachable he was throughout the day, taking the time to meet and speak with everyone. Hearing about the impact the Henderson Family Foundation has had on so many students was inspiring and made the evening feel very personal and welcoming. A message from Professor Hanifa Shah OBE during her welcome speech that really stayed with me was to never forget the opportunities we have been given and to look for ways to give back to our communities in the future. I’m proud to share that I'm 1 of only 3 winners of the Cal Henderson Innovation Seed Fund, receiving £5,000 funding for my Final Year Project across all computing courses at Birmingham City University. (Please find attached my pitch video for the Combi Live idea) My project, Combi Live, is a solution focused on improving Peru’s semi-formal public transportation system, combining real-time information and surveillance to deal with everyday issues such as safety, overcrowding, unreliable arrival times and the lack of emergency alert systems. Having moved to the UK at 17 as an international student to study Computer Science, this project is deeply personal. Growing up in Peru, I experienced first-hand the ongoing problems in public transport and heard countless testimonies from family and friends, especially women, about daily harassment, robberies and the absence of rapid response mechanisms. These challenges have persisted for years with little meaningful improvement. When given the opportunity to choose my own dissertation topic, I didn’t hesitate. Combi Live aims to contribute to safer, more reliable public transport, starting in Lima. I'm grateful to my supervisor Waldo C. for his guidance throughout the process. This funding will allow me to take Combi Live to the next level and present it at BCU Innovation Fest 2026.

I designed an app to support the creative community in the West Midlands For my final-year UX Design module, I created Exhibitly, a mobile app that helps local artists connect with independent venues like coffee shops and small businesses. The idea is simple: • Venues list the spaces they have available and describe the type of artwork they are looking for. • Artists can browse these opportunities and send a collaboration request to venues. • Venues can also discover artists through the app and invite them to collaborate. • Once a collaboration is agreed, the artist can display and sell their work through the venue, with a small commission handled by the app. For example, a coffee shop looking for warm, seasonal artwork can discover an artist whose style fits their atmosphere, and artists can also reach out to venues by sending a collaboration request to display their work for a set period. I have attached some early figma prototype screens. They follow accessibility guidelines, key UX laws and common visual design standards used in the UK. For educational purposes, I used real West Midlands businesses and artwork from different artists. I also featured my sister’s coffee shop in the Jewellery Quarter, Alterna (Instagram: alternajq), as one of the example venues. If you are an artist or someone with strong creative work who wants to gain exposure, display your art in a real venue and potentially sell it with a small commission agreed directly with Alterna, feel free to reach out. I would love to share more details.

6 Months as a Systems Developer at Birmingham City University 😄 Six months ago, I started my industrial placement year at Birmingham City University as a Systems Developer within the College of Computing. Since then, I’ve had the opportunity to work on various applications and projects that support both staff and students, leveraging Power Apps, SharePoint, and Python (Pandas). I’ve also had the chance to assist in innovation project sessions with first-year students, helping to discuss and develop ideas for their module. Performance Monitoring for Assessments: My first project using using Power Apps involved enhancing an application that allows staff to monitor, manage, and upload assessments across different modules. I focused on improving its design and scalability, ensuring that it remains a valuable tool for years to come. A notable achievement was identifying a low-performing assessment, where, after intervention, the submission rate improved from 75% to 94%. Tutor Allocation System: Alongside my colleague Abdullah Kholwadia, we developed a system using Python and Pandas to accurately allocate tutors to over 2000 students. By ensuring that tutors were matched based on relevant staff data. Student Engagement Tracking System: Building on the tutor allocation data, I developed an application from scratch using Power Apps to help staff monitor student engagement. This system allows tutors to track their tutees, log key interactions, and identify students who may need additional support. What I’ve learned so far: -Project management skills, balancing multiple tasks effectively. -Clear and effective communication, especially when sharing ideas and collaborating. -Teamwork and mutual support, working alongside colleagues. -Professional discipline, from problem-solving to adapting to a structured work environment. I’m grateful to everyone at work who has supported me throughout my placement, especially my line manager Waldo C. for his guidance.

Attended the AI Symposium on 16-17th December at Birmingham City University 🤖 I had the opportunity to assist and enjoy multiple presentations. A big thank you to Haitham Mahmoud and Shaheed Parvez ✪ for the invitation and for letting me lend a hand while also learning so much from the event. There were some incredible projects showcased, including one by my colleagues Jack Devey and Palvir Singh Gill, who presented their published paper, "Developing a Smart Wireless Sensor Network for Waste Management in Cities." Amazon’s presentation on generative AI through AWS, demonstrated how they are enhancing AI with new features, products, and machinery to serve hundreds of thousands of users daily. We also had esteemed guests from Astana IT University in Kazakhstan, who showcased a project aimed at recognizing handwritten text with high accuracy. They trained their AI using over 30,000 images of their students’ handwriting to capture different styles. The symposium covered a wide range of industries where AI is making a difference. The event was well-organized by the team led by Faisal Saeed, and co-organized by Sameer Barmansoor, Haitham Mahmoud, Associate Professor Edlira Kalemi Vakaj, Iain Rice, Mohamed Medhat Gaber, Nouh Sabri Elmitwally, Rehan Bhana, Shadi Basurra, and the entire organizing team Abdullah Kholwadia, Mohammad Qasim, Jack Devey, Bright Asare Bediako, and others who contributed to its success. I hope to attend the next AI Symposium and, hopefully, present a project of my own in the future! 👀

Reflecting on a Great Learning Opportunity 🙌 Over the past two months, I had the opportunity to work as a Feasibility Study Research Assistant at Penta Pattern & Model Ltd with Professor Javaid Butt and under the guidance of Ishver Patel. This engineering micro-placement was truly insightful, especially for someone coming from a computer science background. Throughout my time here, I gained hands-on experience with the Instron machine and learned essential safety practices and testing methods. This included measuring Dimensions, Hardness, and Surface Roughness on various polymer samples, which involved special preparation steps like heating in high-temperature ovens and sand exposure. I then performed Three-Point Bending and Tensile Testing to capture critical data, including maximum force (kN), displacement at break (mm), and other key material properties. Working through multiple tests allowed me to achieve accurate results and record data systematically in Excel, comparing samples across various temperatures and time intervals. This experience gave me a new perspective on the challenges within engineering, and I’m looking forward to exploring further opportunities in this field. 🙌

🌟 Last week, I had the incredible opportunity to participate in the Innovation Fest at BIFCA in Wuhan, China. The event was a showcase of creativity, technological and unique projects that highlighted the ambition and hard work of each team. I was impressed by the rich culture of Wuhan. The city's infrastructure, food, traditions and even music left me shocked. As a music enthusiast, witnessing and participating in the local music scene was a particularly memorable experience. Playing the piano at the Innovation Fest closing ceremony was a moment I'll never forget. Another highlight of the trip was collaborating with students from Wuhan Textile University. We supported their projects and shared wonderful experiences outside the university, despite their busy schedules. One of the most memorable experiences was participating in an English class where we exchanged thoughts about our education and learnt about student life in Wuhan. This incredible experience wouldn’t have been possible without the amazing support from BCU professors and staff. Special thanks to Richard Davies, Benjamin, Zee, and everyone else who was there to assist us. It was also a pleasure to journey alongside four great students from the College of Computing: Charanpreet Kaur, Harriet Rottan, Seehem Mosaid and Arthur Cosslett. Additionally, our leaders and guides, Roy Priest and Gerald F. were fantastic with their patience (especially since I lost my passport on the first day in Wuhan 😅 but luckily got it back) and enthusiasm throughout the trip. Last week has definitely changed me for the better, and I can’t wait for the next opportunity to visit Wuhan, China again. Thank you all for making this an unforgettable experience! 🌟 #InnovationFest #Wuhan #BCU #WUT #BIFCA
